AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is treated with dietary modification and/or pharmacologic management with swallowed topical steroids (TS). Swallowed fluticasone propionate (FP) and oral viscous budesonide (OVB) have proven to be effective in resolving symptoms and reversing histologic changes in children and adults with EoE. There are minimal comparative studies between the two agents.

AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: To retrospectively compare endoscopic and histologic outcomes following FP versus OVB therapy in children with EoE in our center.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We performed a retrospective chart review of subjects diagnosed with EoE at a tertiary care center between 2010 and 2015. Inclusion criteria were FP or OVB therapy for ≥8 weeks along with pre- and post-treatment endoscopic evaluation. Demographic and clinical features as well as endoscopic and histologic assessment was recorded for comparative analysis. Histologic response was defined as <15 eos/hpf and remission as <5 eos/hpf.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The study included 68 EoE patients (20 FP and 48 OVB) with a mean age of 10.6 ± 5.2 years (range 1-20 years); 81% were male and 68% were Caucasian. No significant demographic or clinical differences were noted between the two study groups. Overall histologic response to TS's was seen in 44/68 (65%) patients. A significantly greater number of patients achieved histologic response with OVB (36/48, 75%) than with FP (8/20, 40%) (P = 0.0059). Mean pre-treatment peak eos/hpf was 46 ± 19 in the FP group vs. 45 ± 23 in the OVB group. Mean post-treatment peak eos/hpf was 20 ± 29 in the FP group vs. 12 ± 16 in the OVB group (P = 0.002). There was also a significantly greater difference in the change of absolute eos/hpf from pre- to post-treatment in the OVB group (-33) vs. FP (-18) (P = 0.047). A greater number of OVB-treated patients without asthma had a histologic response compared to those with asthma (P = 0.031). The response to OVB was not affected by the delivery vehicle, namely sucralose (Splenda®) vs. Neocate® Duocal.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Our data suggest that treatment with OVB leads to better endoscopic and histologic outcomes than FP. Adherence to treatment and history of asthma are major determining factors in the response to treatments. Using Neocate® Duocal as the OVB delivery vehicle is just as effective as sucralose.
